title: Finally, Mrs. Met gets her due as Mascot Hall of Fame’s newest member
content:
Though it’s been another rough year for the New York Mets, there’s one bright spot to emerge from Flushing: It’s time to make another gigantic bronze bust of an oversized baseball head.

A celebration is in order for Mr. Met’s better half, Mrs. Met, who on Friday became the first female mascot elected to the Mascot Hall of Fame.

Mrs. Met joins her husband, Class of 2007 inductee Mr. Met, whose credentials include bringing joy to generations of fans and also once giving at least one fan the middle finger. Recently, he was caught on camera seemingly celebrating the firing of former manager Carlos Mendoza. But like all Halls of Fame, not all inductees are perfect.

Mrs. Met, of course, does not come with the same asterisks. As the Hall of Fame stated in its news release, the organization “honors the greatest mascots in sports and entertainment and recognizes characters that have made extraordinary contributions to their teams, communities and the mascot profession.”

Mrs. Met initially appeared only in Mets promotional materials and publications. That changed on Opening Day 1975, when she made her first in-costume appearance with Mr. Met. Despite enduring the ups and downs of cheering on a franchise often marked by drama and disappointment, the couple has endured.

Now, they’re in the Mascot Hall of Fame, together.

“Mrs. Met has been a beloved part of the Mets family for decades and has inspired fans of all ages with her energy, kindness and unwavering love for baseball,” said Katie Haas, the Mets’ chief of ballpark operations. “Her election to the Mascot Hall of Fame is a historic milestone, not only for the Mets organization, but for mascots across professional sports. We couldn’t be prouder to celebrate this well-deserved and long overdue honor.”

Mrs. Met joins other notable baseball mascots including Youppi (Class of 2017), the Phillie Phanatic and San Diego Chicken, who were both part of the inaugural class in 2005.
